page: Amazon Web Services c9g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 96 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the c9g.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU score both rank in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 27583.71 GB/sec and large block uncached read bandwidth at 726.85 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput also achieve top-tier status. However, single-core stress-ng performance sits in the middle 50%, and text generation for a small 135M LLM model is relatively weak at 23.25 tokens/sec.

The hardware profile presents specific tradeoffs. While the 192 dedicated physical cores deliver exceptional parallel processing power, the lack of hyperthreading and the absence of AVX or AMX instruction sets may limit certain vector-heavy workloads. Additionally, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage. This server is highly efficient for highly parallelized, compute-bound workloads such as multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, database operations, and Redis caching, where its top-tier multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities can be fully utilized.
